title: MITRE ATT&CK v20 Catalogs AI Abuse, MFA Bypass, Water Utility Attacks
description: MITRE ATT&CK version 20 introduces new techniques and detection strategies addressing AI abuse, multi-factor authentication (MFA) bypass, and attacks on water utilities. The update includes 15 new detection strategies for Enterprise and ICS environments, supported by 38 analytics. Notable additions cover prompt injection attacks on large language models, theft of application-specific passwords to bypass MFA, CAPTCHA bypass methods, and attacks on internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (PLCs) at water utilities. The update also documents threat actor activities, including espionage groups and ransomware operators. These enhancements reflect recent adversary tactics and tradecraft without confirming active exploitation or specific vulnerabilities.
aiSummary: MITRE ATT&CK v20 expands its framework with new techniques and sub-techniques that catalog adversary behaviors involving AI abuse such as prompt injection and misuse of AI agents, MFA bypass via stolen application-specific passwords, CAPTCHA bypass techniques, and attacks on ICS infrastructure, notably water utilities in Minnesota and Mexico. The update replaces deprecated ICS techniques with a consolidated Command and Scripting Interpreter technique and adds command and control traffic hiding methods. It also profiles new and updated threat actors including Nimbus Manticore, Salt Typhoon, APT38, and The Gentlemen ransomware group. The release provides defenders with 15 new detection strategies and 38 analytics designed to improve detection accuracy while minimizing false positives from routine ICS operations. Attribution of some ICS attacks remains unconfirmed.
aiImpact: The additions to the ATT&CK framework enhance defenders' ability to detect and understand adversary tactics involving AI systems, MFA bypass, and ICS attacks, particularly on water utilities. While the framework update itself does not represent a direct vulnerability or exploit, it reflects evolving adversary techniques that could impact enterprise and industrial control systems. The documented ICS attacks caused operational lockouts at water utilities, indicating potential disruption to critical infrastructure. No confirmed active exploits or CVEs are associated with this update.
